# Top 10 Test Scenarios (Ranked by Risk)

| # | Scenario | Risk | Rationale |
|---|----------|------|-----------|
| 1 | Submit after selecting a suggestion via click, then verify all 8 FR-05 fields are persisted with correct types/formats (boolean, ISO local timestamp, BCP-47 locale). | **Critical** | Data-contract violations are silent — the UI shows "Success" even if the backend persists corrupt/wrong-typed data, directly risking downstream systems that consume this record (billing, analytics, compliance). |
| 2 | Verify `start_date`/`end_date` are recorded in the **user's local time** (IST, UTC+05:30), not UTC or server time. | **Critical** | Timestamp correctness is foundational for any time-based reporting/SLA; a silent UTC-vs-local mismatch is exactly the kind of defect that passes functional testing but breaks production. |
| 3 | Prefix-match filtering (FR-02): typing a string that matches no suggestion's prefix removes all suggestions from the list. | **High** | Core, default, always-on business logic — most first-time users will hit this path immediately; a broken filter breaks the primary UX of the whole feature. |
| 4 | Form submission with invalid input (no valid suggestion selected/typed) shows the error message and does **not** persist a record with `completed: true`. | **High** | If invalid submissions silently succeed on the backend, downstream systems get corrupted "completed" records — a data-integrity risk, not just a UI glitch. |
| 5 | Match-Anywhere mode (FR-03) enabled: typing a substring that appears mid-string (e.g., "method") keeps all matching suggestions visible, including ones that don't start with it. | **High** | This is a backend-configurable mode — if untested, a config toggle could silently break the default experience for any tenant/environment where it's enabled. |
| 6 | Selecting a suggestion via click correctly populates the input field with the exact suggestion text (no partial/trimmed/duplicated text). | **Medium** | Common source of subtle UI bugs (extra whitespace, wrong list item bound on click) that directly corrupts the `text` field in the data contract. |
| 7 | Suggestion list updates correctly on rapid/successive keystrokes (debounce correctness) without flickering or showing stale suggestions. | **Medium** | Real users type fast; a race condition here causes visibly wrong suggestions and can lead to selecting the wrong item. |
| 8 | Tab-key navigation moves focus logically: input → suggestion list → Next button, and Enter/Escape behave as expected at each stop. | **Medium** | Accessibility/keyboard-only usage is a common enterprise requirement; broken tab order blocks an entire class of users and is easy to regress silently. |
| 9 | API response schema validation — confirm no extra/missing fields beyond the FR-05 contract, and reject malformed payloads (missing field, wrong type) with a clear error rather than a silent 200. | **Medium** | Contract drift between frontend and backend is a common integration bug source, especially across releases when either side changes independently. |
| 10 | Locale field reflects full BCP-47 format (e.g., `en-IN`) rather than a bare language code (e.g., `en`), for a user in India. | **Low** | Cosmetic/data-quality issue in isolation, but compounds into real bugs downstream if any consuming system does locale-based formatting (dates, currency) keyed off this field. |

**Ranking logic:** Critical = silent data corruption reaching production with no user-visible symptom (1–2). High = breaks primary user flow or lets bad data through with some detectability (3–5). Medium = real but narrower-blast-radius functional/UX bugs (6–9). Low = data-quality/cosmetic issues unlikely to cause immediate incidents (10).
